sentences.sentence: NICE says acute sore throat is often caused by a viral infection, and most people get better without an antibiotic.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Only a University Hospitals Sussex A&E leaflet text said sore throats are usually caused by viruses like colds or flu, less often bacteria; nhs.uk page text for this was not returned. NICE NG84 says acute sore throat is often caused by a viral infection.

sentences.sentence: A University Hospitals Sussex NHS leaflet lists tonsillitis, laryngitis, strep throat and glandular fever as other common causes of a sore throat.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Sussex leaflet lists tonsillitis, laryngitis, strep throat and glandular fever as other frequent causes. Search said it found nothing on smoking as a cause.

sentences.sentence: NICE suggests scoring tools (FeverPAIN or Centor) to spot people with a sore throat who may be more likely to benefit from an antibiotic, and these include fever, pus on the tonsils, tender neck glands and no cough.

sentences.sentence: A sore throat usually clears up on its own and often lasts about a week.

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales says a pharmacist can advise about paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain, and a hospital trust leaflet notes that not everyone can take ibuprofen safely.

sentences.sentence: NICE says most people with a sore throat will not need an antibiotic.

sentences.sentence: NICE says a scoring tool (FeverPAIN or Centor) should be used to identify people with a sore throat who may be more likely to benefit from an antibiotic.

sentences.sentence: A GP can often diagnose tonsillitis from the symptoms and a look at the throat, a swab can show whether bacteria are the cause, and a blood test for glandular fever is recommended if symptoms are severe or will not go away.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS tonsillitis: GP can often diagnose from symptoms and a look at the throat; a swab can show if bacteria are the cause; glandular fever blood test recommended if symptoms are severe or will not go away. The swab is not tied to severity.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says glandular fever is most common in people aged 15 to 24.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS glandular fever page: most common in people aged 15 to 24. The symptom list was not in retrieved text.

sentences.sentence: Antibiotics do not work for glandular fever because it is caused by a virus.

sentences.sentence: Quinsy is a collection of pus between the tonsil and the wall of the throat, and is a complication of tonsillitis.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS tonsillitis: quinsy is a pocket of pus (abscess) between the tonsil and the wall of the throat, a complication of tonsillitis. 'Rare' not shown.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to contact a GP practice if a sore throat has not started to improve after a week, and to ask for an urgent GP appointment or call NHS 111 for a very high temperature, feeling hot, cold or shivery, or a weakened immune system.
